title.en: The new Mrs Pearson faces the family

hook.en: Doris wants her dress ironed, Cyril wants his tea and George wants to go to his club. This evening, "Mrs Pearson" has other plans.

objectives.en: Describe the confrontations with Doris, Cyril and George
Explain how humour exposes the family's selfishness
Discuss the role of the "new" Mrs Fitzgerald

narration.en: Doris wants her dress ironed, Cyril wants his tea and George wants to go to his club. This evening, "Mrs Pearson" has other plans.

body.en: When Doris asks her mother to iron her dress before going out with Charlie Spence, the new "Mrs Pearson" refuses and mocks her choice of boyfriend. Cyril finds nothing ready for him and is told that from now on his mother will keep fixed hours like any worker. Both children are shocked and hurt.

points.en: Doris: no ironing; Charlie Spence mocked
Cyril: no service; mother will work fixed hours

narration.en: When Doris asks her mother to iron her dress before going out with Charlie Spence, the new "Mrs Pearson" refuses and mocks her choice of boyfriend. Cyril finds nothing ready for him and is told that from now on his mother will keep fixed hours like any worker. Both children are shocked and hurt.
A before-and-after table shows the role reversal at the heart of the comedy.

say.en: Before, she would iron Doris's dress; now she refuses.
Before, she served Cyril; now she will keep fixed hours.
Before, she feared George; now she tells him home truths.
Before, quiet and polite; now bold, smoking and drinking.

body.en: George comes home expecting to go to his club, but "Mrs Pearson" tells him bluntly that people there laugh at him behind his back. She drinks and smokes and will not be ordered about. Meanwhile, "Mrs Fitzgerald", with Annie's gentle nature inside, is upset to see her family treated so roughly.

points.en: George is told he is laughed at in the club
New "Mrs Pearson" drinks, smokes and talks back
New "Mrs Fitzgerald" (Annie inside) worries for her family

problem.en: How does the new "Mrs Pearson" deal with Doris?

steps.en: Doris expects her dress to be ironed.
Mrs Pearson refuses and tells her to do it herself.
She also mocks Doris's boyfriend, Charlie Spence, leaving Doris in tears.

answer.en: When Doris demands that her dress be ironed, the new Mrs Pearson flatly refuses and tells her to do it herself. She also makes fun of Charlie Spence, and Doris, shocked by her mother's change, bursts into tears.

points.en: The new "Mrs Pearson" refuses to serve Doris and Cyril and mocks Doris's boyfriend.
She deflates George by telling him he is laughed at in his club.
Role reversal exposes the family's selfishness in a comic way.
